category: Q&A knowledge API (REST, JSON) with quarterly XML data dumps

free_tier.stated: With no key, 300 requests per day per IP. A free app key from Stack Apps raises the daily limit to 10,000 per IP; an access token gives a separate 10,000-per-day quota for each user and app pair, up to 5 per user. Every site's content is also published quarterly as an XML data dump.
free_tier.notes: A keyless call answered 200 with quota_max 300. When one IP uses several keys, the highest key's limit applies to that IP, so more keys do not add quota. Anonymous paging stops at page 25: a page above 25 answered access_denied with no key or token.

per_object_cap.stated: at most 100 items per page and 100 ids per {ids} parameter; page numbers above 25 need an app key or an access token

retention.stated: the API serves the live sites; the official dump page offers the current quarterly dump, and Academic Torrents lists community uploads of the network dump from 2024-02-29 to 2026-09-30
retention.notes: The company states it will keep the dumps online for as long as reasonably possible.

egress.terms: Free: API responses are gzip-compressed JSON with no byte price; the official dumps download free from a logged-in profile, and the community copy on the Internet Archive downloads over anonymous HTTP with Range support

interface_detail: JSON over HTTPS GET at https://api.stackexchange.com/2.3/, every response compressed; OAuth 2.0 for user-scoped calls and writes; quarterly XML dumps as one 7z archive per site, downloaded from the profile settings (per site, or the whole network since October 2026); the Stack Exchange Data Explorer runs SQL over a copy refreshed every Sunday.
tooling: Any HTTP client that decompresses gzip; 7-Zip or p7zip for the dump archives; a BitTorrent client for the Internet Archive and Academic Torrents copies of the network dump.
chaining: The quarterly XML dump is the bulk path for a whole-site or whole-network read (official download from a logged-in profile, or the anonymous community copy on the Internet Archive and Academic Torrents); the API at 300 requests a day keyless, or 10,000 with a free key, serves fresh lookups; the Data Explorer answers SQL over the weekly copy.

limits.value: 300 requests per day per IP with no key; 10,000 per day per IP with a free app key, and an IP using several keys gets the highest key's limit
10,000 requests per day for each user and app pair with an access token; up to 5 such quotas per user
more than 30 requests a second from one IP are dropped, with a ban on the order of 30 seconds to a few minutes
a response carrying backoff means that method must not be called again for that many seconds; semantically identical requests at most once a minute
100 items per page and 100 ids per call; page numbers above 25 need an app key or an access token

limits_note: The keyless quota is shared by every keyless application on one IP. The network-wide dump download is reported to fail around 19.5 GB for some downloaders.
binding_note: An IP gets 300 requests a day with no key and 10,000 with a free key, so a whole-site read goes to the quarterly dump, which has no request count.

identity_cost.detail: Keyless reads need nothing: a call with no key answered 200 at 300 requests a day. The 10,000-a-day key needs an application registered on Stack Apps, whose registration page sends a visitor to the login page; the network signup takes an email and a password, or a Google or GitHub sign-in. The official dumps need a logged-in profile on the site; the community copy on the Internet Archive needs no account.

reliability_note: The network-wide dump came back in October 2026 after a removal of about two years, and downloads of the full archive are reported to fail around 19.5 GB; the Internet Archive copy is a community upload, not an official release.
confidence_note: The quotas and throttles are documented, not exhausted. A keyless call answered 200 with quota_max 300, page 26 with no key answered access_denied, and a HEAD on one site archive of the Internet Archive copy answered 200 with its size. The 10,000-a-day key quota sits behind a sign-up.
